meta.purpose: Inputs for splitting m8_v4's 6 blocs into 17 actors (v7). Data only, no model code changed.
meta.value_format: {value, unit, year, source, confidence (high/medium/low), verified (fetched this session), note}; 'judgment' in note marks estimates

actor_names.WEU: Western EU (EU-14 + CY, MT, CH, NO, IS)
actor_names.SEA: Southeast and other East Asia (ASEAN, TL, MN, DPRK, Pacific, PNG)

membership_notes: Membership as specified. Judgment calls: Sudan -> SSA; Western Sahara -> MENA; Pacific and Caribbean territories in SEA/LAC; 13 European/Atlantic microstates (Andorra, Monaco, Liechtenstein, Faroes, Greenland, Gibraltar, etc., 0.7M people) unassigned.

US.name: United States

labor_force.source: ILOSTAT modelled estimates (ILOEST, Nov 2025 vintage), DF_EAP_2EAP_SEX_AGE_NB total 15+, https://sdmx.ilo.org (same series as WB SL.TLF.TOTL.IN)

core_workforce.source: ILOSTAT modelled employment by ISIC4 (DF_EMP_2EMP_SEX_ECO_NB) 2025; H share of H+J from latest national LFS (DF_EMP_TEMP_SEX_ECO_NB)

social_expenditure_pct_gdp.unit: % GDP, public social expenditure incl. health, population-weighted

social_expenditure_pct_gdp.note: GDP-weighted (WB NY.GDP.MKTP.CD 2024): 19.8. ILO excl.-health pop-weighted: 16.8. Data years 2024-2024 (latest per country). Pop coverage 100%. SOCX values are lower than ILO incl.-health totals for the same countries (e.g. US SOCX 2024 19.8 vs ILO 2022 26.4), so OECD vs non-OECD actors are not perfectly comparable.

gov_effectiveness_pctile.source: World Bank WGI 2026 update (data year 2025), GOV_WGI_GE.EST (api.worldbank.org source=3); percentile computed by us from rank of estimate among 213 economies, since the revised WGI API no longer serves GE.PER.RNK
gov_effectiveness_pctile.note: WGI GE score (new 0-100 scale) pop-weighted: 76.7. Pop coverage 100%

state_capacity_class.note: judgment: high >=70th pctile, medium 45-70, low <45 (pop-weighted). Share of actor population living in countries >=70th pctile: 100%

ai_compute_share.unit: share of global installed AI compute (H100e), by location
ai_compute_share.source: https://epoch.ai/data/gpu_clusters.csv (Epoch AI GPU clusters dataset, downloaded 2026-10-16; last entry 2025-07; non-superseded H100e by country) ; https://epoch.ai/data-insights/trends-in-ai-supercomputers
ai_compute_share.note: Epoch GPU-cluster dataset aggregation (computed this session; data to mid-2025; covers ~10-20% of global): 0.7680. Epoch headline (verified): US ~75%, China ~15% (Mar 2025). 2026 value is judgment adding China smuggled chips (median 660k H100e = ~1/3 of China total, so ~2M of ~20M global), Malaysia/Johor build-out, Stargate UAE first 200MW due 2026 (still under construction per Epoch Jul 2026).

US.automation_notes: Robotaxi: Waymo ~400-500k paid rides/week early 2026, 14M trips in 2025, target 1M/wk end-2026 (secondary, unverified). Not in GlobalData top-4 for autonomous haul trucks. Robot installs led by automotive (13,500); food +30%, logistics/warehousing growing. Most robots imported from JP/EU.

Ankara summit 7-8 July 2026 reaffirmed Art. 5; overshadowed by renewed US-Iran strikes and Turkey F-35 push; European allies+Canada raised core defence spending ~USD 139bn in 2025
Oct 2025: US stopped rotation of a brigade with elements in several eastern-flank states; ~1,000 US troops remain in Romania

May 2026: Pentagon announced ~5,000-troop cut tied to Germany after Trump-Merz feud over Iran war; armored BCT deployment to Poland and a long-range fires battalion to Germany cancelled; SACEUR says more withdrawals to come (US Europe presence ~80,000)
Trump called NATO 'a paper tiger' (spring 2026) and chided European allies for refusing to back the US-Israeli war on Iran / help reopen Hormuz

Greenland: 17 Jan 2026 Trump announced 10% tariffs (rising to 25% in June) on 8 allies (DK, NO, SE, FR, DE, NL, FI, UK) that sent troop contingents to Greenland; force not ruled out; 21 Jan reversed after Rutte 'framework' at Davos
Later 2026: reported US-Denmark-Greenland security deal giving US permanent basing/overflight while preserving Danish sovereignty, signing expected at UNGA pending parliaments
reliability_evidence.note: single aggregator; not confirmed by primary source

reliability_evidence.claim: Art. 5 invoked once (after 9/11, 2001)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Ratified treaty, integrated command, nuclear sharing and forward forces keep it the strongest arrangement in the set; but the guarantor (US) has openly coerced a member over territory (Greenland), cut forward forces in 2025-26 and used troop posture to punish political disagreement. Intra-European legs are strengthening (5% pledge, French/UK nuclear moves). Strength varies by dyad: US->Baltics/Poland lower than UK/France->Poland now.

arrangements.name: EU mutual assistance clause, Art. 42.7 TEU

members.WEU: EU members (all WEU except Switzerland, Norway, Iceland)
members.EEU: EU members (Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Romania, Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania)

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: if a member is 'the victim of armed aggression on its territory, the other Member States shall have towards it an obligation of aid and assistance by all the means in their power', without prejudice to neutral members' policy and NATO primacy (background)
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: no formal; French 'dissuasion avancée' (Mar 2026) offers a European dimension outside EU structures

reliability_evidence.claim: Invoked only once (France, Nov 2015)
March 2026 Shahed drone strike on RAF Akrotiri (Cyprus) during Iran war; Cyprus did not formally invoke 42.7; Christodoulides demanded an operational playbook; Commission preparing a 'guiding plan'
EU reportedly rejected Cypriot expectation of 42.7 activation (July 2026)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Legally stronger wording than Art. 5 but no command structure, no operational plan yet, neutral carve-outs, and the 2026 Cyprus episode showed reluctance to activate. Rising as EU defence-industrial programmes grow.

arrangements.name: US-Japan Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security (1960)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes, asymmetric: Art. V each party 'would act to meet the common danger' against armed attack on territories under Japan's administration (covers Senkakus per repeated US statements); Japan's obligation limited by constitution/2015 collective self-defence law (background)
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: yes (US nuclear umbrella; Extended Deterrence Dialogue)

reliability_evidence.claim: Nov 2025 Takaichi said a Chinese use of warships against Taiwan could be an 'existential threat' (collective self-defence trigger); China retaliated (seafood ban, coast guard near Senkakus); US Amb. Glass reaffirmed 'steadfast commitment to the defense of Japan, including the Senkaku Islands'
Jan 2026 Takaichi: alliance would 'crumble' if Japan ignored a Taiwan crisis, but walked back implication of military response; US 2026 threat assessment called her remarks 'a significant shift'

arrangements.strength_rationale: ~54,000 US troops (background), nuclear umbrella, integrated command upgrades, explicit Senkaku coverage reaffirmed under Trump. Discounted for Trump transactionalism and asymmetry (Japan's reciprocal obligation weak).

arrangements.name: US-ROK Mutual Defense Treaty (1953)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. III each 'would act to meet the common danger in accordance with its constitutional processes' (background)
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: yes (Washington Declaration 2023, Nuclear Consultative Group; background)

reliability_evidence.claim: 28,500 USFK; USFK commander Brunson floated reductions under 'strategic flexibility'; after Germany cut (May 2026) fears USFK next; Seoul MND says no drawdown talks; NDAA reportedly requires current levels
Oct 29 2025 Trump-Lee summit fact sheet includes nuclear-powered submarine cooperation

arrangements.strength_rationale: Tripwire forces and nuclear umbrella remain; drawdown pressure and burden-sharing coercion reduce credibility modestly. ROK obligations outside the peninsula weak.

arrangements.name: Taiwan Relations Act (1979) and Six Assurances
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no: TRA requires the US to provide defensive arms and keep capacity to resist coercion; policy of strategic ambiguity

reliability_evidence.claim: Dec 2025 ~USD 11bn arms package (HIMARS, howitzers, Javelin, TOW, Altius); China sanctioned 20 US firms and 10 executives (26 Dec)
Feb 2026 Trump comments suggested Taiwan's defence 'up for negotiation' with China
May 2026 Beijing summit: Xi asked Trump directly whether US would defend Taiwan; Trump: 'only he knows'; on Six Assurances '1982 was a long way off'; pending ~USD 14bn sale undecided
Late Sept 2026 Xi state visit to Washington: Trump downplayed Taiwan sales to Xi, discussed future Taiwan sales with Xi (contrary to Six Assurances), floated arms sales to China

arrangements.strength_rationale: No treaty; arms flow continued in 2025 but 2026 statements explicitly put Taiwan arms sales on the US-China bargaining table. Japan's posture (Takaichi) adds indirect deterrence.

arrangements.name: ANZUS (1951)

members.CANZ: Australia (NZ: US obligations to NZ suspended since 1986)

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes, weak wording: Art. IV each 'would act to meet the common danger in accordance with its constitutional processes' (background); invoked by Australia after 9/11
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: yes for Australia (declaratory); no for NZ

reliability_evidence.claim: NZ suspension since 1986 nuclear-free dispute; NZ remains Five Eyes partner and 'Pillar 2' AUKUS discussions

arrangements.strength_rationale: US-Australia leg robust (force posture, Pine Gap, AUKUS sunk costs); NZ leg near zero.

arrangements.name: AUKUS (2021)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no (technology/submarine partnership)

reliability_evidence.claim: Pentagon review completed Dec 2025 endorsed AUKUS 'full steam ahead'; at least 3 Virginia-class to Australia early 2030s; review report not public, urges 'critical deadlines'

arrangements.strength_rationale: No defence clause but deep sunk-cost entanglement that raises credibility of ANZUS and UK presence in Indo-Pacific.

arrangements.name: Five Eyes (UKUSA intelligence)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no (intelligence sharing)

reliability_evidence.claim: Reported temporary US pause of intelligence sharing with Ukraine (Mar 2025) shows intel is used as leverage

arrangements.strength_rationale: Deep institutional integration but not a defence commitment; counts as cohesion signal.

arrangements.name: US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty (1951)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. IV 'act to meet the common dangers'; US position that it covers armed attacks on Philippine armed forces, public vessels or aircraft incl. coast guard anywhere in the South China Sea

reliability_evidence.claim: US repeatedly reaffirmed Art. IV coverage of the South China Sea incl. coast guard; Rubio 'ironclad support' Jan 2025
No 2026-specific US reaffirmation found this session

arrangements.strength_rationale: Explicit grey-zone coverage statements and EDCA sites; never tested against water-cannon level coercion; small forward presence.

arrangements.name: US-Thailand (Manila Pact 1954 / Thanat-Rusk 1962; MNNA)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes in principle (Manila Pact Art. IV, SEATO dissolved 1977 but treaty not terminated) (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: Thailand-Cambodia fighting July and Dec 2025 and renewed 2026 tensions; US brokered ceasefires and provided >USD 100m to Thai army; US also deepening defence cooperation with Cambodia (Colby, Aug 2026) - US acts as broker, not ally-protector

arrangements.strength_rationale: Dormant legal basis, no forward forces, Thailand hedges toward China.

arrangements.name: Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance (Rio Treaty, 1947)

members.LAC: most of Latin America (Mexico, Bolivia, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Venezuela withdrew 2002-2013; background)

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. 3 armed attack on one is attack on all; each to assist (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: 3 Jan 2026 US 'Operation Absolute Resolve' captured Maduro; Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Cuba condemned; US now an intervening power in the region rather than guarantor

arrangements.strength_rationale: No external threat to LAC that would trigger it; treaty functionally dormant; US is the main source of armed pressure in the region.

arrangements.name: CSTO (Collective Security Treaty 1992/2002)

members.RUS: Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan (not Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan)
members.MENA: Armenia (participation frozen since Feb 2024; 'effectively suspended' 1 Apr 2026)

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. 4 aggression against one is aggression against all; immediate assistance incl. military (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: Armenia froze participation Feb 2024 citing failure to help vs Azerbaijan; Pashinyan Aug 2026: no resumption in next 5 years, would welcome expulsion; Lavrov: dues unpaid 2 years, charter provision considered
CSTO did deploy to Kazakhstan Jan 2022 (internal unrest), no member aided Russia in Ukraine

arrangements.strength_rationale: Works as regime-protection for Central Asia and as Russia-Belarus core; failed Armenia test; Central Asians avoid Ukraine war.

arrangements.name: Russia-Belarus Union State; Treaty on Security Guarantees (signed Dec 2024, in force Mar 2025); nuclear deployment
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes (security guarantees treaty including possible Russian nuclear response to aggression against Belarus; background for text)
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: yes: Russian non-strategic nuclear weapons in Belarus since 2023; Oreshnik IRBM unit on combat duty in Belarus from Dec 2025, under Russian command

reliability_evidence.claim: Oreshnik declared on combat duty in Belarus (Russian MoD 30 Dec 2025); Russian ambassador tied it to the security guarantees treaty in force since March 2025; up to 10 systems mooted

arrangements.strength_rationale: Integrated military, Russian forces and nuclear weapons on Belarusian territory; Belarus near-client state.

arrangements.name: Russia-DPRK Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (19 June 2024)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. 4 if either is subject to armed invasion and in a state of war, the other provides 'immediate military and other assistance' per UN Art. 51

reliability_evidence.claim: ~20,000 DPRK troops sent to Kursk from Oct 2024; KCNA (Apr 2025) explicitly justified deployment under Art. 4; ~14,000 still in Russia early 2026, ~7,000 cumulative casualties; engineers/builders deployed

arrangements.strength_rationale: Only 2024-26 pact in the set actually fulfilled in combat (DPRK->RUS). Russian reciprocal defence of DPRK untested but plausible given gratitude and technology transfers; rated 0.75 DPRK->RUS, 0.6 RUS->DPRK.

arrangements.name: China-DPRK Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance (1961)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: Art. II automatic military assistance if either is attacked; China's only defence treaty

reliability_evidence.claim: 65th anniversary marked 10-11 July 2026; Xi-Kim messages; DPRK premier Pak Thae-song in Beijing; Li Qiang urged 'strategic coordination'
Xi visited Pyongyang in 2026 (June or Aug; sources conflict)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Automatic wording, but China signals it would not back DPRK aggression; DPRK pivoted to Russia; ties warming again in 2026.

arrangements.name: China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighbourliness (2001, extended 2021) and 'no limits' partnership (Feb 2022)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no: Art. 9 consultation only when threatened (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: China supplies dual-use goods to Russia but no troops or lethal aid acknowledged; joint exercises continue

arrangements.strength_rationale: Deep economic/diplomatic alignment, no defence obligation; neither would fight for the other over Taiwan or Ukraine.

arrangements.name: GCC Joint Defence Agreement (2000) and Peninsula Shield Force

members.GULF: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: aggression against any member is aggression against all (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: During 2026 Iran war, Iran struck Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi; Gulf states intercepted mostly with own systems, issued joint condemnations
Peninsula Shield used once in Bahrain 2011; Qatar blockade 2017-21 shows intra-GCC rupture risk

arrangements.strength_rationale: Real but thin collective capacity; members rely on US and now Pakistan/Turkey rather than each other.

arrangements.name: Saudi-Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (17 Sept 2025) -> Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Turkey (7 Aug 2026)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: 'any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both'; Mecca pact: armed attack on one is attack on all; Fidan: 'technically the same' as NATO Art. 5; text unpublished
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: ambiguous: Saudi official said 'all military means'; Pakistani minister hinted then denied nuclear umbrella; Belfer calls umbrella speculative

reliability_evidence.claim: SMDA signed 17 Sept 2025 in Riyadh, after Israeli strike on Doha (9 Sept)
Reuters (18 May 2026): Saudi invoked SMDA during Iran war; Pakistan deployed >=8,000 troops, 16 aircraft (mostly JF-17), 2 drone squadrons, an HQ-9 battery
reliability_evidence.note: seen via Wikipedia summary of Reuters, not Reuters directly

reliability_evidence.claim: Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed 7 Aug 2026 by MBS, Erdogan, Sharif; secretariat in Saudi; first ministerial committee Istanbul 31 Aug 2026; Pakistan: no expansion planned

arrangements.strength_rationale: Rare case of a new pact being activated within months (Pakistani deployment). Credible for Pakistan->Saudi (defensive deployments, paid); Saudi->Pakistan against India much less credible; Turkey's NATO membership creates conflicting obligations.

arrangements.name: US-Qatar security guarantee (Executive Order, 29 Sept / 1 Oct 2025)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: unilateral: 'policy of the United States to guarantee the security and territorial integrity of the State of Qatar against external attack'; 'all lawful and appropriate measures' incl. military; executive order, not Senate treaty

reliability_evidence.claim: EO issued after Israeli strike on Doha; Axios: less binding than treaty
March 2026: Gulf officials (AP) frustrated/angry US had not defended them enough vs Iranian strikes, interceptor stocks depleting; Qatar intercepted missiles and downed 2 Su-24s itself

arrangements.strength_rationale: Al Udeid basing makes US involvement near-certain if Qatar attacked, but EO is revocable and 2026 showed US prioritising Israel/own forces.

arrangements.name: US-Saudi Strategic Defense Agreement (18 Nov 2025) and MNNA designation
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no published clause; vague 'regional deterrence' language, weaker than the Qatar EO

reliability_evidence.claim: SDA signed at MBS White House visit; Saudi named MNNA (4th GCC state after Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar); F-35s and ~300 tanks
Saudi invoked Pakistan pact, not US, during 2026 Iran war

arrangements.strength_rationale: Arms-and-basing relationship with vague guarantee; Saudi hedging via Pakistan/Turkey.

arrangements.name: US-Bahrain Comprehensive Security Integration and Prosperity Agreement (C-SIPA, Sept 2023)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: consultation and deterrence commitment, not a treaty guarantee (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: Bahrain (US 5th Fleet HQ) struck by Iran in 2026

arrangements.strength_rationale: 5th Fleet presence gives de facto tripwire; executive agreement.

arrangements.name: US-Israel (no treaty; de facto: QME law, 2016 MOU USD 38bn, joint operations)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no formal

reliability_evidence.claim: US and Israel jointly attacked Iran from 28 Feb 2026; ceasefire Apr 2026, interim deal 17 Jun, collapse in July, renewed US strikes
Gulf officials: US operation focused on defending Israel and US troops

arrangements.strength_rationale: Strongest de facto US commitment outside treaties; US fought alongside Israel in 2025 (June strikes, background) and 2026.

arrangements.name: Japan-Philippines Reciprocal Access Agreement (signed Jul 2024, in force 11 Sept 2025)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no (status-of-forces/access)

reliability_evidence.claim: Entered into force 11 Sept 2025; Japan's first such agreement in Asia

arrangements.strength_rationale: Enables joint training; no defence obligation.

arrangements.name: Japan-Australia (2022 Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation, RAA 2023, Mogami frigate deal)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no: consult on contingencies (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: 18 Apr 2026 contracts for 3 Japan-built upgraded Mogami frigates (of 11), ~A$10bn programme, first delivery 2029

arrangements.strength_rationale: Quasi-alliance with industrial lock-in; no automatic defence.

arrangements.name: UK-France Northwood Declaration (10 July 2025) and French 'dissuasion avancée' (Île Longue speech, 2 Mar 2026)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: political: 'no extreme threat to Europe that would not prompt a response by our two nations'; UK-France Nuclear Steering Group
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: partial/emerging: Macron offered temporary deployment of nuclear-armed aircraft to allies, partner participation in nuclear exercises, first warhead increase since 1992; complementary to NATO

reliability_evidence.claim: Northwood text and Steering Group
Macron 2 Mar 2026 Île Longue speech: forward deterrence, temporary deployments, warhead increase, coordinated with Washington
Actual deployment agreements with specific host states after March 2026

arrangements.strength_rationale: Significant new European nuclear signal but declaratory, small arsenals (~290 FR + ~225 UK, background), no treaty.

arrangements.name: France-Poland Treaty of Nancy (9 May 2025)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: mutual assistance 'including by military means' in case of armed aggression on their territories; additional to NATO/EU
arrangements.extended_nuclear_deterrence: no explicit (Poland seeks inclusion in French dialogue)

reliability_evidence.claim: Signed in Nancy, Europe Day 2025; similar to French treaties with Germany, Italy, Spain

arrangements.strength_rationale: Bilateral reinforcement of NATO/EU obligations; untested.

arrangements.name: Joint Expeditionary Force (UK-led) and UK-EU Security and Defence Partnership (May 2025)

members.WEU: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden

arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no (JEF is a framework for coalition operations); UK-EU partnership no defence clause (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: UK leads NATO forward land forces in Estonia (background)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Operationally useful, reinforces NATO northern flank; no obligation.

arrangements.name: Pakistan-China 'all-weather strategic cooperative partnership'
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no treaty

reliability_evidence.claim: Pakistan's ~80% of arms imports from China; Chinese J-10C/PL-15 used in May 2025 India-Pakistan clash (background)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Arms supplier and diplomatic shield; China would not fight India for Pakistan.

arrangements.name: India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no

reliability_evidence.claim: Putin Dec 2025 visit to Delhi: trade target USD 100bn by 2030, defence cooperation; Russia remains India's largest defence supplier, S-400 final deliveries pending; US 50% tariffs on India 2025, Feb 2026 deal tied tariff cut to ending Russian oil

arrangements.strength_rationale: Arms dependence, not an alliance.

arrangements.name: Quad (US, Japan, India, Australia)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no

reliability_evidence.claim: India-hosted leaders' summit stalled amid US-India tariff dispute; no confirmed 2026 leaders' summit found

arrangements.strength_rationale: Consultative; damaged by 2025 US tariffs on India.

arrangements.name: Five Power Defence Arrangements (1971)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no: consultation in case of attack on Malaysia/Singapore (background)
arrangements.strength_rationale: Consultative, exercises only.

arrangements.name: Ukraine security guarantees (bilateral security agreements 2024; proposed US guarantee; 'coalition of the willing')
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: no (bilateral agreements pledge assistance, not defence); US guarantee reportedly '100% ready' in Jan 2026 but WSJ: no commitment to direct military assistance; requires peace deal first

reliability_evidence.claim: Jan 2026 Zelensky: US guarantee 100% agreed, awaiting signing and ratification; 10-year term; does not commit US to direct military help
Oct 2026 no general ceasefire; Rubio: settlement currently unattainable; talks scheduled in Miami; NATO Ankara summit approved support through 2027

arrangements.strength_rationale: Large aid flows (now mostly European-financed purchases of US arms) but no one is obliged to fight for Ukraine.

arrangements.name: Alliance of Sahel States (AES) confederation (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger; 2023 Liptako-Gourma Charter)
arrangements.mutual_defence_clause: yes: attack on one is attack on all (background)

reliability_evidence.claim: Left ECOWAS Jan 2025; rely on Russian Africa Corps (background)

arrangements.strength_rationale: Mutual junta support against insurgency and ECOWAS; low capacity.

us_reliability_cross_cutting.claim: 7 Jan 2026 presidential memorandum withdrawing US from 66 international organizations (35 non-UN, 31 UN entities) incl. UNFCCC, IPCC, UN Women, International Law Commission, International IDEA; follows EO 14199 review
us_reliability_cross_cutting.note: No security alliance on the list per reporting seen; signal of general disengagement from multilateral commitments

us_reliability_cross_cutting.claim: Greenland tariffs on 8 NATO allies (Jan 2026), threatened force, then reversal
Troop posture used punitively: Germany ~5,000 cut after Trump-Merz feud (May 2026); Romania brigade rotation ended (Oct 2025); USFK reduction debate
Taiwan arms sales discussed with Xi (2026), contrary to 1982 Six Assurances
Gulf partners complained US did not defend them adequately in Iran war (Mar 2026)
Countervailing: US kept Art. 5 language at Hague and Ankara, endorsed AUKUS, approved record Taiwan package (Dec 2025), extended new guarantees to Qatar/Saudi, fought alongside Israel
Tariffs on allies: 2025 reciprocal tariffs (EU, Japan, Korea deals with investment pledges), 50% on India (2025)
us_reliability_cross_cutting.note: only India figure checked this session

alliances.pair_matrix_convention: Key 'A->B' = judged strength (0-1) of A's commitment to come to B's armed defence in 2026, combining legal obligation, forward presence, nuclear umbrella and recent behaviour. For multi-country actors the value is a population/strategic-weight blend of member-level commitments (see note). Pairs not listed = 0.0 (no meaningful commitment). All judgment.

base_rates.finding: Alliances reliable 74.5% of the time (1816-1944, coding fulfilment against the specific obligations in each treaty); earlier estimates (~25%) reflected mismeasurement

base_rates.study: Berkemeier & Fuhrmann (2018) 'Reassessing the fulfillment of alliance commitments', Research & Politics 5(2)
base_rates.finding: Overall fulfilment 50% (1816-2003); 66% before 1945, 22% for 1945-2003; by type: defence pacts 41%, nonaggression 37%, offensive 74%, neutrality 78%
base_rates.note: Post-1945 rate rests on few wartime cases; FFI (2023) argues war-only dichotomous coding understates reliability

base_rates.study: Leeds (2003) 'Do Alliances Deter Aggression? The Influence of Military Alliances on the Initiation of Militarized Interstate Disputes', American Journal of Political Science 47(3): 427-439, doi:10.1111/1540-5907.00031
base_rates.finding: Defensive commitments to a potential target reduce the probability that a challenger initiates a MID; offensive-support and neutrality pacts increase it. Exact effect sizes not retrieved
base_rates.note: Contested: Kenwick, Vasquez & Powers (2015, JOP) find no deterrent effect post-1945; Leeds & Johnson reply (2017)

base_rates.study: Fuhrmann & Sechser (2014) 'Signaling Alliance Commitments: Hand-Tying and Sunk Costs in Extended Nuclear Deterrence', American Journal of Political Science 58(4): 919-935, doi:10.1111/ajps.12082
base_rates.finding: Formal defence pacts with nuclear states 'appear to carry significant deterrence benefits' (fewer militarized challenges to protégés, 1950-2000), but forward-deploying nuclear weapons on the ally's soil adds no further deterrent effect

base_rates.study: Leeds & Savun (2007) 'Terminating Alliances: Why Do States Abrogate Agreements?', Journal of Politics 69(4): 1118-1132
base_rates.finding: Alliances are more likely to be opportunistically abrogated (ended in violation of terms) when members' power, external threat, or domestic political institutions change, i.e. when the original bargain no longer fits; not all terminations are abrogations. Specific percentages not retrieved
base_rates.source: citation only (journal page 403; secondary mention in GSU thesis https://scholarworks.gsu.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/b25ffb54-f2be-4142-8b7d-93c2d7d245bc/content)
base_rates.note: Finding from background knowledge; do not use a numeric abrogation rate from this study until checked

base_rates.study: Leeds (2003) 'Alliance Reliability in Times of War', International Organization 57(4): 801-827
base_rates.finding: Changes in members' power or domestic policymaking processes strongly predict failure to honour commitments

alliances.suggested_model_use_of_base_rates: Use 0.5 (Berkemeier-Fuhrmann overall) as the prior probability that a formal defence commitment is honoured if triggered, ~0.4 for defence pacts specifically, ~0.75 as an upper bound where the treaty language precisely fits the contingency (Leeds et al.). Leeds-IO finding implies discounting dyads where guarantor's domestic politics changed sharply (US 2025-26). Fuhrmann-Sechser supports giving the nuclear-umbrella treaties (US-JP, US-KR, NATO) a deterrence bonus regardless of forward-deployed weapons.
caveats: All strength numbers are analyst judgments, not measured quantities.

methods.pop_labor_social: Population: UN WPP 2024 medium variant, year 2026, summed over member locations from the official WPP CSV (thousands -> billions); world total 8.3007 bn. Labor force: ILO modelled estimates (ILOEST) 2025, total 15+, pulled from sdmx.ilo.org (identical to WB SL.TLF.TOTL.IN, which also has 2025). Taiwan is included in ILOEST. Ukraine, Lebanon, Palestine, Sudan, South Sudan lack 2025 ILOEST: latest available ILO year scaled by WPP population ratio (judgment). Kosovo: judgment from KAS LFS 2024 rates. Small territories not in ILOEST: actor LF/pop ratio (judgment). Core workforce: ILO modelled employment 2025 by ISIC Rev.4 section: B (mining) + C (manufacturing) + D-E (utilities) + F (construction) + H (transport/storage). ILOEST only gives H+J combined, so H = (H/(H+J) share from the latest national LFS in ILOSTAT, default 0.70 when absent) x (H+J). Plus a flat 4% of employment for repair/maintenance, security services and core admin (judgment; 3-5% range shown in notes). Social expenditure: public social expenditure incl. health, % GDP. OECD SOCX (public, all programmes, latest year 2022-2024) for SOCX members; ILO World Social Protection Report 2024-26 Annex 6 'total expenditure on social protection including healthcare' (latest year, mostly 2020-2023) for others (parsed from the report PDF). Aggregated population-weighted (WPP 2026); GDP-weighted (WB 2024 current USD) shown in note. Government effectiveness: WGI 2026 update (data year 2025). The revised WGI no longer publishes percentile rank through the WB API (GE.PER.RNK returns 'invalid'), so percentile = share of the 213 economies with a lower GE estimate (0-100), which matches the WGI percentile-rank definition. Population-weighted. New 0-100 governance score also reported. Class thresholds (judgment): high >=70, medium 45-70, low <45.
